- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., >68.00); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion: if 3–5 consecutive days show price below 62.00, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.3–0.7% to forecast for next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to overcorrect; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.0% in next 2–3 periods.
